data.about: Nervi's Burgo paper mill is a suspension roof: the deck hangs from a 16-panel funicular cable spanning the two pylon tops, and the back-stay cables run down to the deck edges, where the deck itself is the tie that takes the horizontal pull. The pole of the force diagram comes from the classic half-sag trial: chords through the doubled sag point give parallels through the load-line ends. The concrete columns lean exactly along the resultant of cable pull, hanger load, own weight and back-stay pull — drag the sag or the anchors and watch them tilt.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: the built factory; 25 dotted lines of action divide the main span D–E in 16 and each back span in 4; dash-dot rails mark the draggable sag Z₃ and anchor W
steps.title: The site: Nervi's suspension roof

steps.caption: left: the deck spans the whole roof at the anchor level (drag W) and carries the distributed load q (green strips)
steps.title: The deck and its load q

steps.caption: left: the main span's load resultant R₁ at midspan — right: the load line: 16 tributary loads stacked tip-to-tail, R₁ = 4 units (drag its top E₃)
steps.title: The resultant R₁ of the main span

steps.caption: left: choose the sag Z₃; the chords D–A₄–E through the DOUBLED sag (grey, dashed) — right: parallels to the chords through the ends of the load line meet at the pole (a funicular polygon of a uniform load sags half its resultant triangle)
steps.title: The sag and the trial chords

steps.caption: right: rays from the pole to every load-line division — left: from Z₃ outward, each cable side parallel to its ray: the funicular lands exactly on D and E
steps.title: The cable

steps.caption: left: at every line of action a hanger drops from the cable to the deck — right: each carries one tributary piece of the load line R₁
steps.title: The hangers

steps.caption: left: each back span carries the resultant R₂ — right: its own load line: ⅛ + ¼ + ¼ + ¼ + ⅛ = 1 unit from Q₄ (drag it)
steps.title: The back-span load R₂

steps.caption: left: the trial chord W–D (grey, dashed) — right: halve the load line (grey ½ marks), draw the parallel to the chord through the midpoint: the pole sits where it cuts the horizontal through the bottom
steps.title: The back-stay pole

steps.caption: left: from the anchor W up to the pylon top D, each side parallel to its ray; hangers pick up the back span — right: the force triangle closes: C = pole→top pulls at D, D = bottom→pole is the HORIZONTAL pull the deck takes as a tie
steps.title: The left back stay

steps.caption: left: the mirror image up to E, with the tie pull F at W′ — right: the mirrored triangle: R₂, E and F
steps.title: The right back stay

steps.caption: left: the cable pulls back with A′, the back stay with C′, the pylon hanger hangs Q on the head, and the column weighs wCC — right: laid off tip-to-tail from H₅
steps.title: The forces on the column head

steps.caption: right: the polygon closes: G balances A′ + Q + wCC + C′ — left: the column axis (dashed) is drawn PARALLEL to G through D: reactions G and H at the feet
steps.title: The column force G

steps.caption: left: Nervi's tapered columns built around the axes — lean them by dragging the sag Z₃ or the anchor W: the axis always follows G
steps.title: The concrete columns

steps.caption: cable, hangers, back stays and the tie deck resolve pink = tension; the columns blue = compression — click any node (or use the slider) for its equilibrium
steps.title: Tension and compression
